Mrs. Neetu Singh, Advocate, for the applicants.
Mr. A.K. Sah, Deputy Advocate General, along with Mrs. Mamta Joshi, Brief Holder, for the State.
Mr. Shashi Kant Shandilya, Advocate, for the respondent.

The present C482 Application has been preferred by the four applicants, out of which, applicant No.
4 is reported to have died.

The applicant No. 2, who happen to be the members of the society, has made a is concerned, who was then working as a marketing executive, his death will have no consequential effect on the proceedings in C482 Application, as no right would be devolved him or upon the heirs of deceased Manish Dhal.

The applicants in the C482 Application has given challenge to the Chargesheet, being Chargesheet No. 160 of 2018 dated 21.07.2018, as well as the summoning order dated 24.01.2019, as it has been issued by the Court of Judicial Magistrate, 2nd, in Criminal Case No. 165 of 2019 (new number 1963 of 2019), State Vs. Manoj Singhal and others, wherein the present applicants have been summoned for being tried for the offenses under Sections 420 and 506 of IPC.

sentences.text:
It goes without saying, that the two offences, for which the criminal proceedings are being carried against the present applicants are compoundable under Section 320 of CrPC, coupled with the fact,
that this Court has interacted with the complainant, who too has made a statement, that all his grievances now stands settled in terms of the agreement dated 13.02.2023, though the same has been executed on a non judicial stamp paper, but the same is stated to be acceptable by the parties,
who had interacted with the Court during the course of the proceedings.

Since, now the parties to the present C482 Applications have settled their terms as referred to in the said agreement dated 13.02.2023, and particularly, in the light of the fact, that the complainant has made a statement, that all his grievances as of now stand redressed and he doesn't intend to prosecute the present applicants any further, coupled with the fact, that all the offences are C482/913/2021 on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193816223/
1 compoundable under Section 320 of CrPC.
To this proceeding, which has been taken up today, the learned Government Advocate has got no objection, as such.

He submits, that since the offences are compoundable under Section 320 of CrPC, coupled with the fact, that it is dispute interse between the parties to the C482 Application,
the State may not have any grievances, as such, if the Compounding Application is accepted by this Court and the proceedings of Criminal Case No. 165 of 2019, State Vs. Manoj Singhal and others, is permitted to be dropped.

sentences.text:
Owing to the aforesaid statement, coupled with the fact of acceptance of the Compounding Application, which has been duly signed by the parties to the proceedings, as well as by their respective advocates representing their cause, the C482 Application would stand closed and as a consequence thereto, the Criminal Case No. 165 of 2019 (new number 1963 of 2019), State Vs.
Manoj Singhal and others, presently pending consideration before the Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Haridwar, would hereby stand quashed.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.) 22.05.2023 Mahinder/
